questions.questionText: Nine students sit in a row. H occupies the middle seat, J is two seats left of H, and K is three seats right of H. What is K’s position from the right?

questions.questionText: Four boxes W, X, Y, Z are arranged left to right. W is left of X, Y is right of X, and Z is between X and Y. Which order is possible?

questions.questionText: Seven candidates sit in a row. P is at one end, Q is adjacent to P, and R is at the other end. Which position can Q occupy?
questions.explanationText: Because Q is next to end-seated P, Q must be second from that same end.

questions.questionText: A row has ten seats. V is 4th from the left and W is 4th from the right. How many seats lie between them?

questions.questionText: Six friends sit facing north. C is not at an end. A sits immediately left of C, and B immediately right of C. Which three-seat block must occur?

questions.questionText: Five seats are numbered left to right. M cannot sit at an end or in the middle. Which seat can M occupy?

questions.questionText: Eight people A–H face north. H is at the left end; E is immediately right of H; D is 4th from the left; A sits between E and D; B is 3rd from the right with C immediately to B’s left; and F sits left of G in the remaining seats. Who is second from the right?
questions.explanationText: The placements give H–E–A–D–C–B–F–G, so F is second from the right.

questions.questionText: Nine candidates P–X face north. P is in the middle; Q is two seats left of P with R immediately right of Q; S is at the right end; T is two seats left of S with U immediately left of T; V is at the left end; and W sits between V and Q. Who is second from the right?
questions.explanationText: The order is V–W–Q–R–P–U–T–X–S; hence X is second from the right.

questions.questionText: Seven people A–G sit facing south. C is at the physical left end, A is immediately to C’s left according to C, B is immediately to A’s left according to A, and D, E, F, G continue in the same personal-left chain. Who is at the physical right end?
questions.explanationText: Because everyone faces south, personal left is physical right. The chain is C–A–B–D–E–F–G physically, so G is rightmost.

questions.questionText: Two rows of four face each other. North-facing row positions left to right are A, B, C, D. P sits opposite C; Q is immediately to P’s left from P’s south-facing perspective; R sits opposite A; and S occupies the remaining seat. Who sits opposite B?
questions.explanationText: P is in row-2 column 3. P faces south, so Q on P’s left is physical column 4. R is column 1, leaving S in column 2 opposite B.

questions.questionText: Eight employees face north. R, the engineer, sits 4th from the left. M sits immediately left of R. N is 2nd from the right, with the designer immediately right of N. P is at the left end, and P–Q–M form a consecutive block. Who is Q’s immediate right neighbor?
questions.explanationText: R is seat 4 and M seat 3. P is seat 1, so Q occupies seat 2 between P and M; Q’s immediate right neighbor is M.

questions.questionText: Ten trainees A–J face north. F is 5th from the left. B sits three places to F’s right. H is immediately left of B, and A is immediately right of F. Who sits between A and B?
questions.explanationText: F is seat 5, A seat 6, H seat 7, and B seat 8. H is the only person between A and B.

questions.questionText: Eight people sit facing north. K is 2nd from the left. Exactly two people sit between K and L, with L to K’s right. M is 2nd from the right, and N is immediately left of M. Which statement must be true?

N sits immediately right of L

Two people sit between L and M

questions.explanationText: K is seat 2, so L is seat 5. M is seat 7 and N seat 6; hence N is immediately right of L.

questions.questionText: Nine seats are occupied by A–I. E is in the middle. A and I are at the ends. C is exactly halfway between A and E; G is exactly halfway between E and I. If A is at the left end, where is G?
questions.explanationText: A is seat 1, E seat 5, and I seat 9. Halfway between E and I is seat 7, so G is 7th.

questions.questionText: Six people face north in order P–Q–R–S–T–U. First Q and T swap; then the person now in seat 3 moves to seat 5, shifting seats 4 and 5 left. Who finally sits immediately right of S?
questions.explanationText: After the swap: P–T–R–S–Q–U. Moving R from seat 3 to seat 5 gives P–T–S–Q–R–U; Q is immediately right of S.

questions.questionText: Seven candidates face north. B is not at an end. A sits immediately left of B; C sits immediately right of B. D is at the left end and E at the right end. F sits left of A, and G sits right of C. Which three-person block is fixed regardless of the exact open positions?
questions.explanationText: The immediate-neighbor clues force the consecutive block A–B–C. The other relative clues do not guarantee adjacency in the listed alternatives.
